51318-the-prisoner-of-the-mill-or-captai.title: Captain Hayward’S “Body Guard.”
51318-the-prisoner-of-the-mill-or-captai.creator: Lieutenant-Colonel Hazeltine.
51318-the-prisoner-of-the-mill-or-captai.description: A book by Lieutenant-Colonel Hazeltine.. pringfield, Missouri, upon the Wilson creek road, as far as the famous battle-ground rendered immortal by the death of General Lyon, but finding no enemy, it had encamped upon Grand Prairie, a few miles to the west of the bloody field. All in camp was upon the “tip-toe of expectation.” The lovely scene spread out before the view, was sufficient to inspire the heart of man to great and glorious deeds. The broad, rolling prairie lay there, like heaven’s great carpet.

arxiv-1810-08481.title: Large-time asymptotic stability of Riemann shocks of scalar balance laws
arxiv-1810-08481.creator: V. Duchêne, L.M. Rodrigues
arxiv-1810-08481.description: Abstract We prove the large-time asymptotic orbital stability of strictly entropic Riemann shock solutions of first order scalar hyperbolic balance laws, under piecewise regular perturbations provided that the source term is dissipative about endstates of the shock. Moreover the convergence towards a shifted reference state is exponential with a rate predicted by the linearized equations about constant endstates.

arxiv-2011-06270.title: Unique positive solutions to q q -discrete equations associated with orthogonal polynomials
arxiv-2011-06270.creator: T. Lasic Latimer a
arxiv-2011-06270.description: Abstract Boelen et al. [ 3 ] deduced a q q -discrete Painlevé equation satisfied by the recurrence coefficients of orthogonal polynomials and conjectured that the equation had a unique positive solution. We prove their conjecture and discuss related work in the area, highlighting a potentially unifying methodology.

arxiv-2111-02929.title: Mechanism of magnetic diode in artificial honeycomb lattice
arxiv-2111-02929.creator: G. Yumnam 1, J. Guo 1,†, Y. Chen 1, A. Dahal 1, P. Ghosh 1, Q. Cunningham 1, J. Keum 2, V. Lauter 2, A. Abdullah 3, M. Almasri 3, D. K. Singh 1,∗
arxiv-2111-02929.description: Abstract Spin diode is important prerequisite to practical manifestation of spin electronics. Yet, a functioning magnetic diode at room temperature is still illusive. Here, we reveal diode-type phenomena due to magnetic charge mediated conduction in artificial honeycomb geometry, made of concave shape single domain permalloy element.

arxiv-2201-00369.title: Gravitational-wave Emission from a Primordial Black Hole Inspiraling inside a Compact Star: a Novel Probe for Dense Matter Equation of State
arxiv-2201-00369.creator: Ze-Cheng Zou (邹泽城), Yong-Feng Huang (黄永锋)
arxiv-2201-00369.description: Abstract Primordial black holes of planetary masses captured by compact stars are widely studied to constrain their composition fraction of dark matter. Such a capture may lead to an inspiral process and be detected through gravitational-wave signals. In this Letter, we study the postcapture inspiral process by considering two different kinds of compact stars, i.e., strange stars and neutron stars.

arxiv-2403-16609.title: Conversational Grounding: Annotation and Analysis of Grounding Acts and Grounding Units
arxiv-2403-16609.description: Abstract Successful conversations often rest on common understanding, where all parties are on the same page about the information being shared. This process, known as conversational grounding, is crucial for building trustworthy dialog systems that can accurately keep track of and recall the shared information.

arxiv-2405-16665.creator: Eugenio Giannelli, Noelia Rizo, A. A. Schaeffer Fry, Carolina Vallejo
arxiv-2405-16665.description: Abstract . We characterize when a finite group G G possesses a Sylow 3 3 -subgroup P P with abelianization of order 9 9 in terms of the number of height zero characters lying in the principal 3 3 -block of G G , settling a conjecture put forward by Navarro, Sambale, and Tiep in 2018.

arxiv-2409-10252.title: eWAPA: An eBPF-based WASI Performance Analysis Framework for WebAssembly Runtimes
arxiv-2409-10252.creator: Chenxi Mao, Yuxin Su, Shiwen Shan, Dan Li
arxiv-2409-10252.description: Abstract WebAssembly (Wasm) is a low-level bytecode format that can run in modern browsers. With the development of standalone runtimes and the improvement of the WebAssembly System Interface (WASI), Wasm has further provided a more complete sandboxed runtime experience for server-side applications, effectively expanding its application scenarios.

arxiv-2511-09159.title: Rademacher’s Theorem for Calderon-Zygmund-type Spaces
arxiv-2511-09159.creator: T. Lamby
arxiv-2511-09159.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by T. Lamby. Rademacher’s Theorem is a classical result stating that a Lipschitz function on ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} possesses a total differential almost everywhere. This implies that if f f is a function defined on ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} belonging to the Calderón–Zygmund space T 1 ∞ ​ ( x ) T^{\infty}_{1}(x) for every x ∈ ℝ d x\in\mathbb{R}^{d} , then f ∈ t 1 ∞ ​ ( x ) f\in t^{\infty}_{1}(x) for almost every x ∈ ℝ d x\in\mathbb{R}^{d} .

arxiv-2602-21507.title: Conditional Image Diffusion with Interferometric Closure Invariants: Independent EHT Imaging of Centaurus A and 3C 279
arxiv-2602-21507.creator: Samuel Lai ID, Nithyanandan Thyagarajan ID, O. Ivy Wong, Foivos Diakogiannis
arxiv-2602-21507.description: Abstract We present independent imaging analyses of Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observations of the active galactic nuclei in radio galaxy Centaurus A and quasar 3C 279 using Generative Deep learning Image Reconstruction with Closure Terms ( GenDIReCT ), a recently developed machine-learning framework built on conditional diffusion models that uses interferometric closure invariants as primary observables.

pmc-10536719.title: Research Trends of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures in Orthopedic Medical Practices: A Bibliometric and Visualized Study
pmc-10536719.creator: Hongfu Jin, Miao He, Wenqing Xie, Zixuan Xiong, Zhenhan Deng, Yusheng Li, Edgaras Stankevičius
pmc-10536719.description: Background and Objectives: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), also known as self-report measures, are critical tools for evaluating health outcomes by gathering information directly from patients without external interpretation. There has been a growing trend in the number of publications focusing on PROMs in orthopedic-related research.

pmc-11470117.title: Regional tuning of photoreceptor adaptation in the primate retina
pmc-11470117.creator: Aindrila Saha, Theodore Bucci, Jacob Baudin, Raunak Sinha
pmc-11470117.description: Adaptation in cone photoreceptors allows our visual system to effectively operate over an enormous range of light intensities. However, little is known about the properties of cone adaptation in the specialized region of the primate central retina called the fovea, which is densely packed with cones and mediates high-acuity central vision.

pmc-11538529.title: The in vitro effect riboflavin combined with or without UVA in Acanthamoeba castellanii
pmc-11538529.creator: Joohee Park, Choul Yong Park
pmc-11538529.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The anti-Acanthamoeba properties of riboflavin and its enhanced amoebicidal effects when combined with ultraviolet A (UVA) radiation were investigated in vitro. The viability of cultured Acanthamoeba castellanii was assessed by adding varying concentrations (0 ~ 0.2% w/v) of riboflavin to the culture medium or after combined riboflavin and UVA treatment (30 min, 3 mW/cm2) over 1, 3, 5, and 7 days. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were measured following a 30-minute exposure to riboflavin.

pmc-11635637.title: Late mitral leaflet tear after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for acute ischaemic mitral regurgitation: a case report
pmc-11635637.creator: Francesco Cannata, Gloria Tamborini, Marco Zanobini, Ivana Marana, Manuela Muratori, Federico De Marco, Gianluca Pontone, Mauro Pepi, Christoph Sinning, Masahiko Asami, Andrew Harris, Aiste Monika Jakstaite, Nikesh Jathanna
pmc-11635637.description: BackgroundAcute mitral regurgitation due to papillary muscle rupture is a severe complication of acute myocardial infarction. Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is emerging as an effective alternative to surgical treatment, with encouraging outcomes. Leaflet adverse events are rare and are associated with relapse of significant mitral regurgitation.Case summaryA 54-year-old man arrived at our hospital with a late presentation of ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

pmc-11665809.title: Does the type of biomesh influence recurrence in abdominal wall reconstruction? A long-term follow-up to a randomized controlled trial
pmc-11665809.creator: Jaiden Punia, Chad G Ball, Andrew W Kirkpatrick, Thomas Clements
pmc-11665809.description: SummaryThis discussion describes the long-term follow-up of a prospective randomized controlled trial evaluating the performance of the 2 most common biomesh products utilized in the context of complex abdominal wall reconstructions. Although the incidence of hernia recurrence increased over time to 26% (median follow-up 62 mo), both biomesh products performed similarly. Biomesh product choice should remain cost-conscious.

pmc-11728122.title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training on Blood Pressure Levels in Hypertensive Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
pmc-11728122.creator: Luis Romero-Vera, David Ulloa-Díaz, Sergio Araya-Sierralta, Francisco Guede-Rojas, Oscar Andrades-Ramírez, Claudio Carvajal-Parodi, Gustavo Muñoz-Bustos, María Matamala-Aguilera, Darío Martínez-García, Nicola Smania
pmc-11728122.description: Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to (I) evaluate the evidence on the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) in hypertensive patients; (II) determine whether HIIT impacts SBP and DBP differently; and (III) assess the clinical relevance of these effects.

pmc-12431746.title: Impact of CDKN2A gene expression on colon adenocarcinoma via biosignature analysis
pmc-12431746.creator: Chen Xu
pmc-12431746.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Colorectal adenocarcinoma (COAD) has a poor prognosis. Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 2A (CDKN2A) significantly affects the development and progression of various human tumors. However, the significance and pathological mechanisms of CDKN2A in COAD remain to be elucidated.

pmc-12436660.title: Real-time detection of Wi-Fi attacks using hybrid deep learning models on NodeMCU
pmc-12436660.creator: Mohamed Hussien Moharam, Kareem Ashraf, Hussien Alaa, Mostafa Ahmed, Hesham A El-Hakim
pmc-12436660.description: This paper presents a real-time, lightweight system for detecting Wi-Fi deauthentication (DA) attacks that uses the NodeMCU ESP8266 microcontroller for live packet sniffing and feature extraction. Tailored for low-power IoT environments, the system combines the sequential learning capabilities of Long short-term memory (LSTM), Gate recurrent unit (GRU), and Recurrent neural network (RNN) with the interpretability of logistic regression (LR).

pmc-12655272.title: Development of Immunodetection Systems Using a Specific Antibody Against the Recombinant Coat Protein for Detecting Sugarcane Streak Mosaic Virus
pmc-12655272.creator: Intan Ria Neliana, Bambang Sugiharto, Rikno Harmoko, Wahyu Indra Duwi Fanata
pmc-12655272.description: Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV) is one of the mosaic viruses found in mixed infection with two or more viruses. Infections of mosaic viruses show highly similar mosaic symptoms and are difficult to distinguish. This study aimed to develop a specific antibody against SCSMV that could potentially be utilized to differentiate mosaic virus infections.

pmc-13159742.title: From Intention to Action: A Grounded Theory Study on the Staged Mechanisms of Postoperative Exercise Behavior Among Breast Cancer Patients
pmc-13159742.creator: Lihua Shan, Meifen Dai, Xiaoyun Li, Juanya Chen, Jing Yang, Yanyan You, Aiqin Liu, Tianhui You
pmc-13159742.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundExercise is widely recommended for postoperative breast cancer patients due to its benefits for functional recovery and symptom management. However, real-world participation and long-term adherence remain consistently low. Existing research has largely focused on participation rates or perceived barriers, offering limited insight into the behavioral mechanisms that govern how exercise is initiated and sustained over time, particularly within specific cultural contexts.ObjectiveTo explore the mechanisms underlying the initiation and maintenance of postoperative exercise behaviors among breast cancer patients, with particular attention to the

pmc-13248950.title: From Machine Learning to Generative Artificial Intelligence in Urology: Technological Evolution and Future Perspectives
pmc-13248950.creator: Sung-Jong Eun, Jong Mok Park, Yong Gil Na
pmc-13248950.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across healthcare, including disease diagnosis, personalized treatment, and rehabilitation management. In urology, AI research has evolved from traditional machine learning to advanced deep learning and generative models. This review categorizes these developments into 3 primary domains. First, machine learning has been applied to mobile-based platforms for continuous urinary health monitoring and personalized healthcare.

pmc-13411110.title: Frequent emergency department utilization and syphilis case profiles in the Sentara healthcare system: a retrospective cross-sectional analysis in Hampton Roads
pmc-13411110.creator: Martina Zamponi, Grace M. Tillotson, Chandler F. Knox, Mackenzie Tardif-Kunk, Thomas R. Campbell, Peter A. Mollica
pmc-13411110.description: BackgroundSyphilis rates have increased substantially nationwide, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations and individuals with differing patterns of healthcare utilization. The Hampton Roads region of Virginia and North Carolina includes multiple jurisdictions with syphilis rates above the CDC screening threshold, with 7 of its 9 independent cities meeting this criterion.

pmc-13556408.title: 821. Association of Alcohol-Related Genetic Polymorphisms with Problematic alcohol use and Suicidal Ideation
pmc-13556408.creator: Y Nago-Iwashita, T Kanata, M Oba, K Ikeda, D Nishizawa
pmc-13556408.description: BackgroundAlcohol-metabolizing genetic variants, ADH1B rs1229984 and ALDH2 rs671, are strongly associated with drinking behavior (Kranzler et al., 2019) and have also been linked to depressive symptoms (Hishimoto et al., 2010) and suicide-related behaviors (Yoshimasu et al., 2015). Whether these genetic variants modify the relationship between alcohol consumption and mental health outcomes remains unclear.
